question: I want to build a cross-border payment or remittance business on Stellar; which stablecoin and SEP rails should I use, and how should I structure corridors with on- and off-ramps?

golden.answer: Stellar is a fast, low-cost settlement layer, not a complete remittance business. A corridor also needs an on-ramp, KYC, FX quotes, an off-ramp, liquidity, fraud controls and legal cover in each jurisdiction. Rails: SEP-1 discovery, SEP-10 auth, SEP-12 KYC, SEP-6/24 ramps, SEP-31 cross-border, SEP-38 quotes. Choose stablecoins per corridor. Integrate existing anchors first: SEPs guarantee no liquidity, licence or coverage, and costs depend on each anchor's fees and FX.
keyFacts: Stellar is a settlement layer; corridors also need ramps, KYC, liquidity and legal cover.
SEP rails: SEP-1 discovery, 10 auth, 12 KYC, 6/24 ramps, 31 cross-border, 38 quotes.
Pick stablecoins per corridor by issuer, liquidity, redemption, geography and regulation.
Integrate existing anchors first; SEPs guarantee no liquidity, licence or coverage.
avoid: Do NOT give definitive legal or licensing advice for all jurisdictions.
Do NOT imply Stellar removes the need for fiat partners, KYC/AML, liquidity or customer remediation.
golden.notes: Named corridor or provider examples need a dated source; accept any dated, sourced example.

corroboration.claim: Stellar can be a good settlement layer for a remittance business because it gives fast settlement, standardized anchor protocols, and liquid stablecoin rails, but it is not a complete remittance company by itself.
